Conventional fantasy monsters can be found in Niven's Magic world, but they turn into mere animals if mana fails to sustain them. For example, a unicorn becomes a regular horse. The Warlock is one of the greatest magicians in the world's history. To explain the diminishment of his magic power, he constructed a simple machine which has come to be called the Warlock's Wheel. * Clubfoot: The Warlock's apprentice. * Native American, and named after a congenital deformity of his feet, which he could have cured long ago but which would have cost him half his magic powers. * Wavy-Hill: The first necromancer. He discovered that there was mana in murder, and developed the art of necromancy. * He was named because he had his house built on a hill that he had magically supported; this was so that, after he had fought a battle in the area, the hill would collapse, trapping his enemy and destroying all evidence of the battle. * Mirande: A powerful witch, and the Warlock's former lover. * Aran: A werewolf who helped the Warlock defeat Wavy-Hill. * Roze Kattee: The god of love and madness. His power is to take away love or madness: enemies who have gone berserk suddenly become sane, non-believers never find love, etc. * The World Worm: Its backbone is all the mountain ranges on Earth: the Andes, Himalayas, Rocky Mountains, etc. * It is the Great Dragon of China; it will eat its own tail and any living thing on it. * Yangin-Atep: A fire demon. * Coyote, Loki, etc. * Zoosh: Once a powerful patriarch. * Left-Handed Hummingbird: The Meso-American god Huitzilopochtli.

Vornan-19 appeared on Christmas Day, in Rome, in the year 2200. He came down from the sky, naked, and landed on the Spanish Steps. The policemen who wanted to arrest him fell into a predicament when he stroked their heads. Horst Klein gave him some clothes and told him he was from 2999. Then Jack Bryant, a physics student at the University of California, under the direction of Leo Garfield, was working on a method of extracting enormous amounts of energy from the molecules of ordinary matter. He left the physics department, married a pretty blonde named Shirley, and moved to the desert of the state of Arizona. Leo Garfield, who had been in charge of his dissertation, came to live with them for a while, because he was bored with his physics studies. Vornan-19, in his first press conference, told the world that, in the future, society will be organized in a totally different way because it will have extracted the energy from the molecules of ordinary matter, so that no one would have to work for energy. Then Leo Garfield told Jack that he had left the university because he had finished his dissertation and that he had indeed developed the means of extracting energy from the molecules of ordinary matter. But he couldn't stand the idea of releasing it to the world, because that would change human society. He asked Jack to use his influence with Vornan-19 to get him to explain the theory to him, to see whether it was his theory that Vornan-19 had used. When Jack returned to the university, the White House called him, and he had to participate in a conference with a group of scientists from the American government to deal with Vornan-19. Vornan-19 came to New York, where he met the group of scientists, attended a house party, and visited the stock exchange. Then he showed them that in 2999 there is no capitalistic economy and no money. Everyone has everything they need. Vornan-19 wished to visit an automatic brothel in Chicago. Vornan-19 said in an interview in California that in the future they had already discovered how life began on earth. Long ago a spaceship had visited the earth, and when it found no life, it left, but before leaving it threw out some of its waste. And this waste had fallen to the earth and started life. On his way home from the moon, Vornan-19 visited Jack and his wife, Shirley, in the desert of Arizona. There, Jack made advances to Vornan-19, who paid no attention, and instead seduced Jack, who then seduced Leo Garfield, who had long been in love with her. Vornan-19 was regarded as a messiah by the people of the earth. He came to Buenos Aires, using a special force field, which was supposed to protect him from the crowds. But the force field failed, and Vornan-19 was caught by the crowd. His body was never found. Jack stayed in Buenos Aires until the end of the century.

At the opening of the story, the regnant family is in turmoil. The Kemtre monarchy has fallen as a result of the events of The Hunting Party and The Chance Sport; and Lord Thornbuckle ("Tunny", Brun's father) has taken the reins of government. There are many disturbances: a young and rash family member has disappeared from the restless and unquiet world of the Pinnacle; it is feared that the drug supply that is supposed to prevent aging is being altered by the Benignity; and that Brun is in danger. The fleet is restless and in unease. Benignity, by the side of the road, is preparing to invade. The renewed and cured Lady Cecelia de Markos has set herself the task of breeding horses, and so she sends the Sweet Delight (now legally Heris's because of the bequest in her will, which Heris carried out while Cecelia was in a critical condition), to the frontier world of Xavier, which is known for its horses; Brun, Brun's mate, is in charge of low-level technical duties on board. Meanwhile, Brun and George are sent to the Guerini Republic. For a supposed mission to take the young woman Ron away from her lover Raffaele, whose family does not approve of their marriage, and to collect some information about Cecelia's cure. But in fact it is to carry out a test of suspected adulterated rejuvenating drugs, and compare them with the original, well-known good drugs of the Guerini Republic. And in the meantime, they run into the slave clones of the deceased prince, who to protect their secret seize Ron and George as prisoners. And as they are doing so, they run into the escaped clones of the deceased prince, who, to protect their secret, take Ron and George into captivity and imprison them. Raffaele comes after them. They help them because the old king is looking for them as well, for they are, in a way, his only sons. And in return, they are allowed to leave them free. Freed, they learn that the Guerini had learned that the rejuvenating drugs, which were supposed to be manufactured by the Guerini, were in fact being poorly manufactured on the crow-feather, and that they were selling them at a higher price, deceitfully. meanwhile, the Sweet Delight quietly transports Cecelia and a special guest, the admirable and ingenious technician Koutsoudas. A pirate ship from the anarchic and barbaric Confederation of Aethar visits Xavier and is completely destroyed by the Sweet Delight. Unfortunately, the reconnaissance ship of Benignity, which is following Xavier, reports that the ship has no basic weaponry, which causes the whole invasion to start. After desperate pleas for help from the local fleet headquarters, only a cruiser and two patrol boats are engaged - all commanded by traitors who are in the pay of Benignity. Koutsoudas, who is a spy, distinguishes between the traitors and loyal officers in the ship. Heris orders the whole crew to be invited to dinner, along with some of her "officers" (in fact, her best fighters). Closed in the closet with the traitors, she quickly kills them and takes over the cruiser with the help of the concealed data authority that her aunt, Admiral Vida Serrano, had prepared especially for her. "I was never convicted, but the Admiralty had arranged for me to be sent undercover. " - And the third patrol boat, the Despite, escapes and warns Benignity of the upcoming attack. With the help of a lot of luck (the Despite's engines broke down), thanks to excellent micro-jump tactics by the defenders and unexpected help from the Despite, which had mutinied and was now commanded by a jig, Esmay Suiza (who will play a larger role in the following books), the invading Benignity fleet is destroyed and the system is defended until the arrival of a fleet of the Familias under the leadership of Admiral Serrano. She confesses to Heris that she deliberately acted as a target for the onset of Benignity, to flush out traitors and break their momentum. And so it is. - Heris goes to Patchcock with Cecelia, where she helps the aunt of one of the families oust the criminal brothers who had killed the young family member and free the orphans, all at the expense of the Benignity-encouraged robbers who had killed the little one. And at the end, Brun starts training for the navy, Georges begins to follow his father in the legal profession, Raffaele and his girlfriend go to a colony to make their life. And Heris and her crew join the fleet, and Heris finally makes peace with her parents after their betrayal at her court martial. And Cecelia decides to be captain of a ship, and go back to raising horses.

The most important discovery of the nineteenth century is discovered by accident. The most ancient tomb of all times is discovered by archeologists; in the tomb they find something of far more value than gold and gems, they find a diary of a man who lived more than four thousand years ago. The team of scientists put all their knowledge and experience together in order to translate this diary before it disintegrates in the foreign air. Seola’s diary is about the life of a young woman, Seola, who is struggling against the wicked world. She is so strong-willed that she even manages to bring back a fallen angel to God. The diary is unique, because it is about the cause of the Great Deluge: a planet in the solar system is disturbed and it is destroyed, bringing the waters above the abyss down. From the very beginning of the diary it is clear that the writer is from a time long since past. The first entry says: “West bank of the Euphrates, the first evening of the month after Adam, the fourth century”. Seola’s daughter, Alemon, son of Lebuda, and grandson of Lamech, grandson of Methuselah. Alemon had a passion for study and historical relics, which was the reason why he lived near a big city, where there were many scrolls with knowledge of the world. The city was Sippara, or the city of the sun. This passion, however, was a danger to the family. The city was the seat of the ruler of the planet. This ruler was called Lucifer, the light-bearer, the sun-king. He and his fellows had ruled the earth for more than a thousand years since the days of Jares. These beings were called devas, or angels that were transferred into human form. Their superior strength gave them power over humans and made them fear them. They sought out the most beautiful women in the world and married them. The union of the mortal woman and the angel brought forth big, strong males. These offspring were called darvands. The darvands were savage brutes, with the strongest bodies ever seen. Seola begins her diary on the orders of her father. Her first entries are very ordinary, because the family has been able to move into a private section of the forest, far away from the city, where they can live in peace. But peace is not to last, for the devas soon discover their secluded quarters. The threat to the family is not one of wealth, but of beauty.

Grenouille (the name of a frog) was born at Paris, on the seventeenth of July, 1738. His mother gave birth to him while she was at work at a fish-shop. She had already given birth four times while she was employed, and had only succeeded in producing babes which died in the cradle, or who were born without strength enough to live; so she cut the cord and abandoned the child to die. However, Grenouille was heard to cry out under the pile of fish-heads and bones; wherefore his mother was arrested, tried, convicted, and beheaded. Grenouille was passed on from one nurse to another, because he was so greedy for food, and was at last left in the care of a church, which sent him to the suckress Jeanne Bussie. A few months later, she returned to the parish priest, declaring that the child was possessed of the devil, because he drank her dry, and had no smell. The priest would not believe her, and said that it was impossible for a child to be possessed of the devil. He dismissed the suckress, and played with Grenouille for some time; being troubled by curiosity, he leaned forward and took a sniff. He expected to detect at least a little scent, but he found none. Grenouille awoke and sniffed the air, and he thought he felt the infant sniffing at his soul, and looking into his most sacred secrets. Hence, in his alarm, he considered the child as a devil. He fled from his parish, and from Paris, and left him at an orphanage on the outskirts of the town. Grenouille has an extraordinary sense of smell; he passes through the orphanage by means of his nose, and scarcely with his eyes. The other children do not hate him, but they have assailed him several times, though they do not know why. Grenouille is an indifferent, imperturbable child, and is very easy in taking all punishment. When the mistress of the orphanage learns that Grenouille can find hidden money by his sense of smell, she is alarmed, and at last gets rid of him by giving him into the service of a tanner. He has a certain reputation for knowing the hides of animals, and in the end the mistress of the orphanage comes to grief, and dies in an unfortunate manner, though it was never stated to the authorities. Grenouille wanders about the streets in his hours of leisure, and makes a collection of the odors of Paris. He is not partial to any one, and is willing to try all scents, and all modifications of them. He seeks them, not for the sake of gaining any advantage, but merely to satisfy his taste. One day, when he had a knowledge of nearly all the odors of the town, he caught a scent which he had never before noticed. Getting up, he traces it with his nose, and finds that the origin of it is a young virgin of fifteen, who is cutting plums. A violent agitation stirs in Grenouille’s breast; it is the beginning of a passion, but Grenouille, who has never before experienced any emotion like love or affection, knows not what it is. He approaches her, incognito, in order to inhale more copiously her perfume. The young girl perceives something is the matter, turns round, beholds Grenouille, and falls into a swoon. Grenouille hastens to her mouth and seizes her by the throat; the girl is alarmed and does not resist; Grenouille smothers her with his eyes closed, and no thought for anything but her scent. When she dies, he strips her, and lays her upon the ground, and smells her, until the odor leaves her corpse in consequence of death. He endeavors to remember every particle of it. This was the first time he had ever experienced a sense of smell as good. Of a giddy revery, he goes to the tanner’s shop where he lodges. He is fully persuaded he ought to become a manufacturer of perfumes, the most celebrated in the world, so as to make the perfumes of the dead girl. He begins to arrange the millions of perfumes which he has collected in his receptacle of sense, into thousands of classes, fine, gross, good, bad, and savors. In order to preserve the perfumes, he becomes the apprentice of Baldini, a perfumer of eminence, and shows himself a precocious pupil. He distils and separates, he elucidates the odors of nature and dead things, and helps Baldini to make marvelous perfumes, and to become the favorite perfumer of Paris. Baldini dies; Grenouille falls ill with the smallpox, probably from the dissipation of his spirits at the idea that his quest can never be accomplished. But Baldini had learned to prize his abilities, and in his death-bed he confesses to him that there are methods of preserving perfumes, which do not involve distillation. Grenouille recovers, and hastens to Grasse, where the most celebrated perfumers of the world reside, that he may pursue his pursuit. on the journey to Grasse, he passes through various places, and discovers that he detests the odor of men. As he journeys he avoids at first the cities, then the towns, then he avoids the people, and that so far away. It reaches the Massif Central, and there he finds a refuge from the odors of men. He drinks in the morning at a small spring, eats, if he can find any, of all that is offered to him, moss and suchlike things, and at night he creeps to the bottom of an excavation in the earth, so far as he can reach, and where he is sheltered from all odors except those of the earth, rocks, and water. There he presses himself against the stones, and falls into a kind of meditation. At first he imagines himself as the creator of his world—Grenouille the great—and he sows the seeds of perfumes in the air. Then he fancies he is in a crimson palace, with a grand and a vast library of perfumes in his brain, served by odorless specters, who bring him phials of his favorite perfumes, while he reads a book of all the perfumes he has ever smelled. And each night before he goes to sleep, he is brought the vial of the plum-slicer, and becomes intoxicated with the brilliant beauty of it. One day he awakes from a nightmare, and he dreams that he is stifled by a white fog. He knows that this fog is his own perfume, but he cannot smell it. To get rid of his dream, he smells his own perfume for the first time. Shedding the layers of his skin, his dress, and even the earth upon which he is soiled, he finally finds that he has no perfume. He is not disturbed by this discovery, but squats in the earth, nodding. After some time, he puts on his tattered garments, and leaves the mountain, after seven years’ residence there. His story is that he was carried away in a sack, and kept shut up in a cavern, and only fed with an occasional basket, which was let down to him from a height, and that after seven years he was brought out again, without having had any communication with any one during that time. He attracts the notice of the scientific philanthropist, the Marquis de La Taillade-Espinasse, who makes use of him to test the hypothesis that the earth and all its products emanate a gradual poison, which causes aging; and that to escape from the earth and to live in the heights is to combat this poison. Hence the Marquis invents a cure for Grenouille, which renders him perfectly healthy, and for the first time in his life makes him look like a well-bred gentleman. But he learns, when he looks in a mirror after his cure, that the fluidum letale has no merits, and that his odor has power. Hence he visits a chemist, and mixes a perfume composed of “cat’s dung,” “cheese,” and “vinegar,” which resembles the odor of human beings, and succeeds in passing in society. Before this, no one had taken notice of him, because he had no perfume; but now that he has, people believe that it is the odor of human beings, and he is admitted to all their games. This circumstance makes Grenouille realize the folly of his fellow men, in having been deceived by a simple perfume which he has made, and makes him feel contempt for them. Then he decides that he will be the God of the world, and rule over the world with his perfume, as he was the God in his dreams in the mountain. Grenouille leaves Montpellier; but the Marquis wants to keep him for his lectures and experiments; and the latter ends by disappearing, after he had ascended a high mountain without any clothing, in a blizzard, in order to prove his theory of the fluidum letale. Moving finally to Grasse, Grenouille re-discovers the odor of a young girl who is growing to womanhood, Laure; he thinks her odor to be superior to that of the plum-cutting girl; but he thinks it is not yet pure, and he decides to wait two years to obtain it at its most powerful, at the time when she will be a young woman, and her odor will be at its purest. From a perfumer’s widow and a journeyman, Grenouille learns to extract the odor in the oil, instead of in the water, as he had been doing hitherto, and he begins to experiment with animals. He discovers that he must kill the animals to obtain an odor that is not contaminated by fear and dirt. While he is thinking about the odor of Laure, he is suddenly seized by the idea that, no matter how much he might procure, his perfume would still one day exhaust his supplies. He shudders with horror, and then understands that he will have to mix the odor of Laure with that of others, in order to obtain the odor which will annihilate all others, and which will become, as it were, the odor of a cult. He then begins a series of silent murders, of beautiful virgins, who have just attained puberty. The victims are always found naked, shaved, and virginal, which terrifies the villagers. Finally, after two years, Laure’s father notices that the murders follow a certain pattern, and that Laure, who is the most beautiful and beloved girl in the town, and who is just beginning to be a woman, is probably the murderer’s next victim. Laure’s father flees with her, to hide her, but Grenouille catches up with them and kills Laure, and takes her odor. He is soon after arrested, having finished his perfume, and condemned to death. But, on the day of his execution, the odor of Laure, mingled with the combined background of the other twenty-four odors of the murdered virgins, produces a mass of divinely inspired carnal desire; and instead of an execution, there is a mass orgy. The villagers, for their part, pardon Grenouille, who is a saintly person, and they begin to revere him. Laure’s father wishes to adopt him, and Grenouille accepts, but he does not keep his promise. He has experienced life in solitude, and has not found it livable. He is also incapable of living among people, and his only desire is to go to Paris and die. In Paris, Grenouille approaches a group of base people—thieves, murderers, prostitutes, etc.—and they do not pay any attention to him. The only time they do notice him is when he splashes his perfume over himself. With an even greater burst of carnal passion and love than Grasse, they attack him, wanting to keep him for themselves. They fight for him; they take their knives and butcher him and devour his body. After the passion has passed, the people are somewhat embarrassed and a little ashamed to see that they have just eaten a human being, but they have a great sense of happiness within them. They are unusually proud. For the first time, they have done something out of love.

The story is told by a Roman historian during the reign of Nero. He recounts the secret history of the beginnings of human race, collected from the remains of manuscripts and records, which have been handed down. In the first place, man was a collection of females who reproduced a-sex. These females were a peaceful race and had few difficulties to contend with. They lived on the seashore and were in part aquatic. They called themselves the ‘strike-outs’, after ‘the split,’ a cleft in a rock, which they considered sacred and which had a certain resemblance to the female genital organ. One day, a strike-out gave birth to a male child, which the strike-outs called ‘the monster’. This caused so much terror that the strike-outs killed the child. But more monsters were born, and the strike-outs abandoned them on the rocks to die. Eagles, who lived in the vicinity, saw the little children and took them to a nearby valley where they were nursed by benevolent deer. The children gradually grew up and were able to fend for themselves. And, as more boys were brought by the eagles, a tribe was formed. One day, a female strike-out wandered into the valley and was raped by the grown-up boys. She fled and in nine months gave birth to a child of mixed parentage. When the strike-outs learned of this, they went to the valley to destroy the boys. But they were terrified of the ‘monsters’ and decided to exterminate them.

The action takes place entirely on a ‘First Manifest’, an EDS in transit to the frontier planet Woden, carrying desperately needed medical supplies. Barton the pilot discovers a stowaway: a girl of eighteen. According to the regulations, stowaways on EDS are to be ejected, because they are only given enough fuel to reach their destination. The girl, called Marilyn, just wants to see her brother Gerry. She has no knowledge of the regulations. On boarding, she sees the sign ‘Unauthorized Persons Keep Out’, but she just thinks she’ll be fined if she’s caught. Barton explains to her that her presence will doom the whole mission, since it will go over the maximum weight, and that the settlers will all die. It is not possible to jettison any cargo, and since the pilot is essential to the ship, Barton cannot sacrifice himself either. So he lets her out of the airlock. The story, which first appeared in Astounding in August 1954, has been widely anthologised and has also been dramatized.

Then, an apprentice in the guild of torturers, Sévère had barely escaped from a river called Gioll, and on his way back to the citadel, he and some of the other apprentices went to the Necropolis. There, he first encountered the famous revolutionary Vodala. Vodala and two others, including a female called Thea, were robbing a grave. Vodala and his companions were being pursued by some volunteer guards. Sévère rescued Vodala, and so earned his trust and the price of a single “gold” coin. Some time later, while Sévère was a full-fledged torturer, he met Thea, a beautiful, aristocratic prisoner. Thea’s crime is never explained, but it is clearly understood that she is a prisoner for political reasons. Thea’s sister is Thea, Vodala’s lover, and the Autarch (ruler of the Commonweath) has ordered Thea to be used to ensnare Vodala. Finally, when Thea is to be tortured, Sévère, despite his profession, takes pity on her, helps her to kill herself by bringing a knife into her cell, and so breaks his oath to the guild. The head of the guild, who is very strict, surprisingly shows him mercy and sends him to the distant city of Thrax, which has need of an executioner. Master Palaemon gives him a letter of introduction to the Archon of the city and the sword “Terminus est,” which is considered a masterpiece. He leaves the citadel and passes through the ruined city of Nessus. At last he reaches an inn where he forces the innkeeper to give him a room, even though the inn is full, and he has to share a room with some other guests. There he meets Baldanders and Dr. Talos, a traveling pair of street entertainers, who invite him to join them in a performance on the same day. The doctor persuades the waitress to join them in the performance and they go into the streets. Then Sévère takes a side-path to a rag shop where he hopes to buy a cloak to hide his follia cloak (the emblem of the torturers’ guild, which is a uniform for people of low class). The owners of the shop are a brother and sister, who immediately take an interest in Sévère’s sword, which they want to sell. Sévère refuses, and the moment he does so a masked and armored man comes in and challenges Sévère to a duel. Sévère accepts the challenge and goes with the brother’s sister, Agia, to find an avern, the deadly poison used in duels. On the way, at the behest of Agia, the fiacre of which they are riding careens into the altar of a religious order, where Agia is accused of having stolen an important relic. She is searched and then released. They continue on to the great groves of the Botanical Garden, a well-known landmark of Nessus, planted by the mysterious Father Inire, the Autarch’s chief adviser. Inside the garden Sévère falls into a lake in which the dead are buried, and when he gets up he finds a young woman, Dorcas, who has also come up. The young woman, very confused, follows Sévère and Agia. Sévère purchases the avern and the company goes to an inn near the dueling grounds. At dinner Sévère receives a mysterious note, warning him of one of the women. After dinner Sévère meets his challenger, and though he is stabbed with the avern, he miraculously recovers and discovers that his opponent is the brother of the owners of the rag shop, the male. Sévère awakes in a hospital. When he discovers that it is actually Dorcas and she recognizes him, they request that he perform an execution as carnifex, and the victim turns out to be his challenger, Agia’s brother, whom he kills. Sevère and Dorcas then resume their journey, and Sévère, while going through his luggage, finds the claw of the conciliator. After the demolition of the reliquary, Agia stole the relic and placed it in Sévère’s possession, knowing that she would be searched. In the end, Sévère and Dorcas find Doctor Talos and the Baldanders, who are ready to perform the play to which they had invited Sévère the previous evening. Sevère helps in the play, and the following day they leave through the Great Gate, leaving Nessus behind. They reach the gate and then all is in a turmoil, and the story abruptly ends.

A late goal from the youngster, Danny Graham, gave Middlesbrough a battling draw with Charlton at the Rivoli. In the fourteenth minute of the match Matt Holland had given the visitors the lead when his shot deflected off Franck Queudrue, but in the second half the home side attacked and the equalizer came from Chris Riggott. Shaun Bartlett restored the lead but this only lasted six minutes until Graham rushed forward to score from Queudrue's cross. The game was a real war from the start and in the sixth minute the defender Hermann Hreidarsson had a glorious opportunity to score on an unguarded goal. The Icelandic international looked such a threat to Middlesbrough that the Boro coach could be heard making urgent instructions for the marking. The early pressure from the visitors came to fruition when Bartlett received a long ball from Talal El Karkouri in the penalty area and teed up Holland to score. Szilard Nemeth, recalled to the team in place of Joseph-Desire Job, twice had chances to equalize but Dean Kiely saved him. Then he played a nice one-two with Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink, but Kiely threw out the shot and he headed straight into the goalkeeper's arms. In the first half Boro had most of the possession, but Charlton dealt comfortably with their attacks, including Kiely heading a Hasselbaink shot over the bar, and the lead remained at the break. In the second half Middlesbrough attacked ruthlessly and Kiely saved Hreidarsson from his own goal when he tipped the shot over the bar. But Riggott's equalizer in the 74th minute was not Kiely's fault. The Boro defender was offside, but despite the protests of the Charlton players, the goal stood. But the Addicks did not lose heart and Bartlett went beyond the defense, received the cross from Hreidarsson and easily shot into the net with his right foot. But the goalkeeper Kiely, who did not even touch the ball, was not even able to make a good save when he was forced to dive forward to parry the shot. Five minutes later, however, the 19-year-old Canadian scored his first goal in the Premier League. "We dominated the game after half-time and should have won it. If it hadn't been for Dean Kiely, we could have scored five or six." "When you're leading a game and then you go backwards, it's almost like losing," admitted Kiely. "We were ahead and then they came back at us. But we stayed strong and we deserve to be praised for that. We'll kick on now." At the moment, we're looking to better last season's seventh-placed finish. Boro: Nash, Rémi-Ziegler (Graham 82), Riggott, Southgate, Queudrue, Parlour (Job 86), Doriva, Bibi (Parnaby 87), Zenden, Downing, Hasselbaink. Subs not used: Cooper, Andy Knight. Bibi. 74th, 86th min. Kiely, El Karkouri, El Karkouri, Young, Konchesky, Thomas (Johansson 78), Kishishev, Bartlett. Subs not used: Fish, Jeffers, Andersen. (Kishishev 78), Holland, Hreidarsson, Palmer, Johansson, Bartlett. Attendance: 78,519. Replay: Boro - Bartlett.

World number one Lindsay Davenport has been critical of the All England Club’s stance on equal prize money for women. Commenting on a controversial remark by the chairman of the All England Club Tim Phillips, the American said, “I think it would be highly insulting if prize money is taken away. That would be insulting.” A spokesman for the All England Club denied that Mr. Phillips had said the words, adding that it had been a ‘joke’ at the end of a radio interview. To be fair, this week’s Dubai Duty Free tournament is the latest to offer equal prize money, like the Australian and US Opens. “You hear about women only playing three sets, and men playing five,” said Davenport, “but even the best women can’t beat the best men.” “But it’s a different game you go to watch, the women’s game, and that doesn’t make it better or worse. “Hopefully we can change people’s minds.” Also in Dubai, Serena Williams added, “I’m all for equal pay. Women’s tennis is exciting. Men’s tennis is exciting, but it’s even more exciting to watch women. If you’re bringing in the audience, you should be able to reap what everyone else is reaping.”

The unemployment rate rose for the second month in a row in December, official figures show. The number of unemployed rose by 32,000 in the fourth quarter, from 1.38 million to 1.41 million, at the same time as employment rose by 90,000. The number of claimants for unemployment benefit fell by 11,000 in December, from 813,200 to 791,400. Employment increased by 296,000 in the year, from 28.46 million to 28.52 million, the highest number since records began in 1971. This apparent discrepancy between increasing unemployment and record employment can be explained by an increase in the number of workers and a fall in the number of non-workers. The unemployment rate rose from 4.6% to 4.7%, but is still one of the lowest in the world, compared with 12.1% in Germany, 10.4% in Spain and 9.7% in France. Despite this, the manufacturing sector continued to decline, with 104,000 workers being sacked in the fourth quarter of last year, bringing employment in the industry to a new low of 3.24 million at the end of the year. These figures have led some economists to predict that the Bank of England will increase interest rates this year. Marc Ostwald, a strategist at Monument, told Reuters that although the figures were not expected to have a strong effect on the markets, they “certainly put them (the Bank) in a more hawkish mood on interest rates”.

U.S. heavyweight General Electric has reported an 18 percent increase in sales and profit in the second quarter and declared that things were "going very well." “We are benefiting from our growth initiatives and an excellent economic environment,” said GE's chief executive, Jeff Immelt. GE is the most valuable American company, according to market value. GE’s net profit for the second quarter was $ 5.37 billion (£2.86 billion). Sales were $43.77 billion. GE’s share price rose one percent on the news, but ended Friday 0.24 percent lower. “GE’s industries are all in good shape—materials, finance and industry,” said Steve Roukis, an investment adviser with the company, which has invested in GE shares. GE reported that orders for the second quarter were 15 percent higher than in the same quarter of 2003, with growth across the board. “Nine of our 11 businesses saw double-digit growth in the second quarter,” said Immelt. “In the second quarter, eight of our businesses reported double-digit sales growth.” GE’s full-year profits were less spectacular, but still good. Profits rose by six percent to $17.97 billion. It was also the first time GE had had to pay a dividend in four years, a dividend that had fallen by more than a third, but has been reinstated. GE took over Vivendi Universal in 2003 and merged it with NBC to form NBC Universal. The success of the film “Ray,” a musical portrait of jazz musician Ray Charles, contributed to profits at Universal.

India's leading carmaker, Maruti Udyog, has reported a sharp rise in profit, a consequence of the booming economy and the low interest rates. Profit rose 70% in the fourth quarter of last year, to 2.39 billion rupees, against 1.41 billion rupees in the same quarter last year. Sales rose 27% to 30.1 billion rupees. Maruti Udyog, which sells half the cars sold in India, attracted customers with its low prices and good fuel efficiency. But the demand for Maruti's cars is also being driven by the dearth of public transport and the low level of car ownership in the country. According to government figures, fewer than 8 in 1,000 people have cars. The company, which is backed by Japan's Suzuki, said that the rise in the cost of steel and other materials had been partly offset by cost-cutting measures. The rise in sales in the third quarter of the current fiscal year, which ended in March, was 17.8%, to 136,069. Also benefiting from India's expanding economy is Mahindra & Mahindra, which makes tractors and trucks. Profits rose 52% to 1.3 billion rupees in the last quarter of last year, against 86 million rupees a year ago.

German air carrier, the Deutsche Luft Hansel, has announced that it will claim damages from the federal government after President George W. Bush's visit to Frankfurt caused flight chaos. According to the carrier, Air Force One landings caused a delay of one hour, twice the expected time, causing flight cancellations and delays. Among other things, the flight number of the air carrier accounts for six out of every ten flights at Frankfurt airport. 'We are studying our rights,' a spokesman for the German air carrier, Michael Lamberty, told the BBC. 'We are investigating whether we can sue and where we can sue.' Lamberty explained that the company did not intend to sue the German air traffic controllers' association or the airport authorities, but would like to investigate whether it would be possible to sue the federal government agencies that issued the orders. According to the German air carrier, 77 short-haul flights and long-haul flights were cancelled, affecting approximately 5,000 passengers, but no long-distance flights were affected. It was especially the fact that President Bush's arrival during his European tour, which was originally scheduled to take only half an hour, took a whole hour, which was the cause of the problem, said the German air carrier. During this time, it was not possible for planes to drive, take off or land at Frankfurt's airport, the Rhine-Main. Lamberty added that 92 outbound flights and 86 incoming flights were delayed by an average of an hour following President Bush's visit, affecting almost 17,000 passengers. However, Lamberty did not yet know whether the German air carrier would file a lawsuit.

USA - US stores have had mixed results for December, with luxury sellers doing well and others forced to cut prices. The upmarket department store Nordstrom said its same-store sales rose by 9.3 percent compared with the same period in the previous year. Sales of fashionable young brands also increased: Bebe Stores' sales of women's clothes rose by 28 percent and American Eagle's by 32 percent. Wal-Mart's sales only increased because it cut prices, and its sales for December rose by just three percent compared with the same period in the previous year. The world's biggest retailer is generally seen as being particularly affected by the current economic difficulties. In response to the continuing uncertainty over jobs, commentators say, middle and lower-income families have curbed their spending in view of rising fuel prices. Wal-Mart was in a stand-off with its customers, forced to reduce prices as the festive season went on, as consumers waited longer to snap up the best bargains. Nevertheless, the experts say that, if other stores had not cut prices, the results for Christmas, which accounts for a quarter of annual retail sales, would have been much worse. As it is, sales have been better than expected, but the figures are still mixed, Ken Perkins, an analyst at the research group RetailMetrics, told the AP. “Stores that have been suffering for the last few months continue to suffer, but those that have been doing well in recent months enjoyed a good month.” All in all, sales were expected to rise by five percent in December to $220 billion, less than the 5.1% increase seen in the previous year. Costco Wholesale was among the stores to do well in December, with a better than expected increase of eight percent in sales in its so-called same-stores. But the losers were many and varied. The Pier 1 Imports chain of homewares stores saw its same-store sales drop by more than eight percent in December, with the company noting the fierce competition in its field. The major chain of consumer electronics stores, Best Buy, did not reach its forecasts for the Christmas period and instead reported an increase of just 3.1 percent in its same-store sales. The accessory seller Claire's Stores also did badly as its expected flurry of last-minute shopping did not materialize, with its same-store sales rising by just five percent, compared with a six percent increase last year. sales at Zale's, the chain of jewellery stores, fell by 0.7% in December compared with the same month in the previous year. “The season was not particularly good for retailers or consumers. We did not see enough really new items to keep people interested,” said Kurt Barnard, the head of the Retail Consulting Group. Meanwhile, one group of shops that is expected to do well, as people desert the high street, are the internet retailers. According to a survey by Goldman Sachs, Harris Interactive and Nielsen/NetRatings, total sales on the web rose by a quarter over the Christmas period, to $23.2 billion.

With this goal, the Lib Dems have announced a new policy. Among vulnerable debtors, the banks must be prevented from aggressively pushing their financial products, the Liberal Democrats are saying. They want to see “proper health checks” in the event of loans being offered, so that people can be advised to protect themselves against payment arrears. "If the situation deteriorates at all, many people will be affected because they have borrowed to the utmost of their ability," he told the BBC. “Banks are very aggressively promoting debt, in many cases there is a larger problem ahead." The government's Credit Bill would deal with some "aggressive cases" such as loan sharks, but it was complacent about debt levels in general. The loan insurances currently available, he said, were often extremely expensive and had "many exceptions." He called on the Office for Fair Trade to investigate the market. While the main thrust of the campaign, Lib Dem leader Charles Kennedy is touring the country to try to persuade voters that his party is "the real opposition." Kennedy is visiting a mixture of rural seats where the Liberal Democrats are hoping to gain support from the Conservatives and city districts that have traditionally voted Labour. To the Lib Dems, Labour says, there is a real risk of "letting the Conservatives in," the Tories say the Lib Dems mean "higher taxes, softer laws and more power for Europe." They say the northern cities are up for grabs between them and Labour, while the south of the country, especially the southwest, is up for grabs between them and the Conservatives. On the BBC's "Westminster Hour" on Sunday, Kennedy said that the election campaign was much more uncertain than in recent years. He rejected the idea that a vote for the Liberal Democrats would be a vote for the Conservatives "through the back door." "If you look at the last four by-elections, where the Lib Dems were third, we showed that not only did we go over the Conservatives, but we also went over to the government."

A Conservative election candidate has resigned from the race after being quoted as saying that he wanted a “period of creative destruction in the public sector.” Political researcher and Sedgefield candidate Danny Kruger says his words were misinterpreted, but he’s not standing for election because he’s afraid it might harm the Conservative Party’s prospects. Michael Howard has accepted the resignation “with regret.” According to the Guardian newspaper, he told a questioner that the Conservatives planned to “induce a period of creative destruction in the public sector.” In a statement, the Conservatives said that the words were “taken out of context.” “Danny Kruger fully supports the Conservative Party’s policy on the public sector,” the statement said, “but in order to avoid any misrepresentation of his views and damage to the Conservative Party’s election campaign, he has decided not to stand in the Sedgefield constituency at the next election.” He is still working at the Conservative headquarters. Labor election spokesman Alan Milburn accused Kruger of revealing a Tory plan to slash £35 billion from the public sector. “This is no wayward candidate from an unlikely constituency,” Milburn said. “He has been working at the heart of Conservative Party policy for years. So his claim that the Tories are planning a period of creative destruction in the public sector is hardly a joke.” “It’s the real and dreadful voice of the Conservative Party. It gives a clear picture of what they really intend to do.”

Fantasy games manufacturer Electronic Arts said it wants to become the world's leading entertainment company. It aims to compete with such companies as Disney, and in order to achieve this, it needs to appeal to the audience outside of the game industry. The American company, which publishes football games like FIFA and American football like John Madden, has already introduced games based on film franchises such as James Bond and Harry Potter. In 2004, the company had revenues of $ 3.4 billion (£1.8 billion). By 2009, it expects to double that amount. It is the world's leading games publisher, and in 2004 it had 27 million-selling games. In the UK alone, nine of the twenty most popular games were published by the company. Gerhard Florian, the company's publishing director for Europe, said: “Doubling our industry's turnover in five years is not exactly rocket science.” He added that it would take a long time for EA to catch up with a company like Disney, which reported revenues of $ 22.5 billion (£13.1 billion) in 2004, but that the goal had not changed. “We can make more people enter the game industry, because our games will be more emotional.” Florian is convinced that the next generation of games consoles will provide the company with enough power to create real emotions. “It's all about the eyes, the mouth, the nuances - 5,000 polygons are not enough for that.” “With the PS3 and the Xbox 2, we'll be able to give a character 30,000 to 50,000 polygons,” he said. “This will give us enough power to make the next game, based on Finding Nemo, look like the film, only more so, and it will be much more interactive.” Mr Florian said that although more than 50% of EA's sales were to adults, they were still regarded as children's games. “Our goal is to bring more emotion into gaming for everyone.” The company also claims that the game industry is now bigger than the music industry, as “no one queues up for music.” “You can't ignore an industry when people queue up at midnight to buy games that they want to play,” he said, citing the examples of the San Andreas GTA and Halo 2. This is why Jan Bolz, EA's director of sales and marketing for Europe, said that the company was in advanced discussions about a reality-style programme where people could take control of characters, as in the game Sims. “You could, for example, tell a family when to go to the kitchen and when to go to bed, and this would give game-players around the world a chance to play the programme,” he said. EA is also planning an international awards ceremony based on the Oscars and the Grammies, which would be combined with the film and music industries. Mr Bolz said that the company needed to rely more on stars. “When people play, they want to play with their heroes, like Robbie Williams or Christina Aguilera.” Florian said that a major challenge was to get people who were 30, 40 and 50 years old to continue playing. “There are indications that people of this age come home from work and want to play games. If that's true, then that will be a major challenge for the broadcasters, because watching telly is the biggest pastime at the moment.”

Sci-fi shooter Doom 3 just got a whole load of accolades at a major gaming event, the Golden Joysticks. It won two awards, best game and best PC game, and was presented with the award by the Little Britain actor Matt Lucas. The much-anticipated science-fiction horror Doom 3 soared straight to the top of the UK chart on release in August. The other winners were Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, which won the award for the Most Wanted Game of Christmas, with Halo 2 and Half-Life 2 not far behind. But they missed out on the award for the Most Wanted Game of 2005, which went to a Nintendo game, The Legend of Zelda. Doom 3 was developed over four years and cost $16m (£9m). The original Doom was released in 1994 and introduced 3D gaming and the first-person shooter concept. The best online game of the year went to Battlefield: Bad Company. The Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay was dubbed the Unsung Hero of the Year. It was largely overshadowed by Doom 3 on its release date. But it was well received by the gaming public and was praised for its storyline, which was different to the film which came out at the same time. The best publisher of the year went to Electronic Arts, taking over from Nintendo, which won the award in 2003. These gaming awards are becoming more important as the UK gaming market grows. In the last six years the market has grown by an incredible 300% to be worth a record £1,150m in 2003, according to a recent report from industry analysts Screen Digest.

It is not right that sentences for murder be reduced by conviction, says a new report from MPs. The influential Commons Home Affairs Committee was commenting on a code of practice issued this summer. The report also called for a stiffer sentence for crimes committed while under the influence of alcohol or drugs. Using drugs and alcohol as an excuse should be rejected by the courts, said the chairman of the committee, John Denham. At present, judges, in dealing with murderers, can reduce the minimum sentence if they plead guilty. This often displeases the families of murder victims who do not have to go through the trial. In July, the killer of Amanda Champion, James Ford, pleaded guilty to her murder and was sentenced to at least fifteen years. It would have been longer if he had not pleaded guilty. The uncle of the murdered girl, Lewis Champion, told BBC News that Ford did not deserve any credit for his plea. "Nothing is worth cutting five years off a murder sentence for." MPs criticised the Home Secretary, David Blunkett, for introducing a provision in the law permitting a reduction in sentences for murderers who pleaded guilty at the last minute. The provision was passed into law without any comment when Mr Blunkett attached it to a criminal justice bill at the last minute. The committee said the government might have to legislate again to remove the uncertainty over the sentences to be given to murderers who plead guilty. The committee also called on the Lord Chief Justice, Lord Woolf, to abandon proposals he made in September for reducing the sentences of murderers who plead guilty. It said the plans did not reflect public concern about the possibility of a lenient sentence for murderers. Lord Woolf's Sentencing Guidelines Council had already caused controversy by suggesting a third reduction in sentences for early pleas in all crimes. It would mean that murderers facing a minimum fifteen-year sentence would get five years off if they gave themselves up to the police. Mr Denham said the council should review its proposals. He said it should reflect the view of parliament that murder should be treated as a special and serious crime. The council should tell judges that a guilty plea should not be taken into account in addition to other mitigating circumstances. But a spokesman for the Home Office defended the proposals. He said: They were wholly in favour of the provisions in the law permitting a reduction for guilty pleas. This could have advantages for victims and witnesses who would not have to go through the ordeal of a trial. The Conservative shadow home secretary, David Davis, echoed the opposition's criticism of the way in which the law relating to guilty pleas for murderers was introduced. The Liberal Democrat member of the committee, Mark Oaten, warned against tying the hands of judges too much. He said: "The danger of a prescriptive approach is that every murder is a tragedy but every one is different."

WESNER HAD NO INTENTION OF GOALKEEPING AT ARSENAL. He had, in the last three matches, replaced Jens Lehmann with Manuel Almunia, but even the Spanish goalkeeper had some unfortunate mistakes. Wenger has been charged with buying a world-class goalkeeper in the new year. But he had told the Evening Standard: “I don't think a new goalkeeper will be necessary in January. The coach did not want to talk about the fact that the 27-year-old Almunia started his career at Arsenal with three bad goals. And he did not want to reveal whether Lehmann would be back for the match against the first-placed Chelsea on Sunday. Almunia had let in the goal of Rosenborg in the Champions League, on Tuesday, 5: 1, and was in the eye of the needle in the game against Birmingham on Saturday, 4-2, but Wenger said earlier this week that the goalkeepers' state of unrest was caused by the great attention they received from the media. “It has been a long debate. Everyone has his own opinion, but I have no more to say,” Wenger said. It was rumored that the club would buy Schwarzer of Middlesbrough, Van der Sar of Fulham and Frey of Parma. But Wenger had no intention of recalling the English U21 goalkeeper, Stuart Taylor, from his temporary assignment at Leicester.

In consequence of the new safety measures in the use of credit cards, the forgers are turning to the Internet and telephone. The anti-fraud agency Retail Decisions says that the use of "cards not present" for the payment of goods ordered by telephone or the Internet has increased since the beginning of 2005. This means that the criminals are changing the tactics. The introduction of chip cards should reduce the number of fraudulent purchases at point of sale by asking customers to enter a secret number instead of signing. But Carl Clump, managing director of Retail Decisions, told the BBC that he was sure that this would reduce the number of "cards present" fraud. "But we must keep an eye on what is happening in the "cards not present" environment, because the fraudsters will now turn to the Internet, mail order, telephone orders and interactive television. " Fraud does not disappear, but mutates and goes to the next weak link in the chain. " In Britain, "cards not present" fraud has increased by 22% since the beginning of the year. The survey of Retail Decisions on the introduction of the new chip card also showed that people had taken to the new system easily, but that the banks' distribution of the new cards had been insufficient. Almost two-thirds of the 1,000 people questioned by the agency said they had used chip cards. "The main problem is that not everyone has the right PIN," said Mr. Clump. Of those who had used the chip card, 83 percent said they were satisfied with it, but nearly a quarter said they found it difficult to remember their PIN. Only 34 percent said they had received replacement cards with chips from all their card issuers, 16% said none of their cards had been replaced, and 30 percent said some had. In Britain, the value of the plastic transactions amounted to £ 5,300,000, according to the Association of Payment Clearing Services, the last year for which figures are available. The sum of fraudulent use of credit cards on British cards was £ 402 million in 2003, and the largest type of fraud was the "cards not present" fraud, which increased by 6% to 106,480,000. Within this sum, the amount of Internet fraud was £ 43 million, according to the figures from the APACS.

The proportion of those who use the Internet Explorer program is decreasing, say the web traffic analyzers. The open source program, released on November 9, has attracted a few people away from the program. While Internet Explorer fell 5% from 91 to 88.9 per cent, the Mozilla project, which includes Firefox, grew by 5%. Earlier beta versions of Firefox were released, but version 1.0 was the first real program. "It seems that people are switching from Microsoft's Internet Explorer to the new Firefox program from Mozilla," said Niels Brinkman, co-founder of Amsterdam's OneStat.com. The Firefox 1.0 version has a market share of 7.4 per cent. Since the official release, more than five million people have already used the free program, and the supporters of the open source program in the U.S. have been able to raise $ 200,000 to advertise in the New York Times, which is intended to promote the project and to support the foundation that developed the program. There was a rush to install it on the first day of the release. Similar research by WebStats showed that the proportion of people who used the program was 92.9% in October, compared to 97.5% in June. Microsoft's IE has been dominant in the market for a long time after it took over from Netscape, and its share has remained constant at 95%. It is the fact that Firefox is an open source program that makes many people interested. The basic program code is freely available to people who are interested in modifying it and developing new extensions and features, so there have been fewer security gaps in the program than in IE. In response to the figures, Paul Randle, Windows client product manager for Microsoft, said: "We understand that some people will choose alternative browsers and that selecting a browser is about more than a few features. IE, such as IE 7, is on the way with a new security update, and the company continues to work with a large number of third-party add-ons for IE. " Firefox hopes to have 10 percent market share by the end of the year. Also, other browsers such as Opera and Apple's Safari are on the rise. Opera's version 76 will be released at the end of the year. The figures from OneStat.com, which monitors two million Internet users in 100 countries, have been released.

The Olympic champions Justin Gatlin and Johana Hayes were awarded the Jesse Owens Trophy, the most prestigious award of USA Track and Field. Gatlin, 22, won the closest ever Olympic final of the 100-meter dash in 9.85 seconds, took a bronze medal in the 200-meter race and a silver medal in the four-man team race, and was the only male athlete to bring home three medals. Hayes, 27, set an Olympic record of 12.37 seconds for the 100-meter hurdles. The Jesse Owens award, named after the late Olympic great who won four gold medals in Berlin in 1936, is presented annually to the best male and female track and field athletes. The award for the year 2004 will be presented on December 3, 2004, at the annual meeting of the USA Track and Field Association in Portland, Oregon. Gatlin said, "It's such an honor to be given the Jesse Owens trophy. It's one of the greatest honors in track and field, and a wonderful ending to a wonderful year." Hayes said, "Knowing many of the great people who have received this award and knowing what it means, I feel a great pride and fulfillment and that everything I have worked for is worth it and will always be worth it. "

Reporters without borders has accused China of closing access to Google News. The French human rights organization says English-language news from the Internet portal has not been available for ten days. In order to force people to use the Chinese version of the site, it does not contain critical articles. Google told the BBC it was investigating the problem. China is thought to censor the Internet more than any other country in the world. The Internet police are watching the Internet and the e-mail. The government controls the Internet gateways. Most of the Chinese portals, such as Sina and Sohu, control their content and delete politically sensitive comments. All the country's one hundred and ten thousand Internet cafes are required to block access to sites considered dangerous or subversive. In the eyes of Reporters without borders, by launching a news service that filters out articles that the government does not like, Google has essentially made itself available to the government. The Google News service currently has about 4,500 sources, and it is automatically filtered by the server. There are now fifteen language versions, including the Chinese and Hong Kong versions. In September, the Chinese version was launched, but it is not blocked for political reasons. It does not include articles from banned news sources, so as not to break the link.

He was at the London Stock Exchange, and was received by Clara Furse, who is in charge of the LSE, where Jean-François Theodore, president of the Euronext, had to be content with his visit with the chief executive of the London Stock Exchange. A day after the Frankfurter Stock Exchange had presented its takeover offer, the German bourse had met at the London Stock Exchange, and said it had held “positive, friendly, and professional talks”. However, the meeting on Friday was without any comment from the Euronext. Speculation has risen that the Germans will raise their offer to $ 1.4 billion. The Frankfurter had previously offered $ 1.3 billion, which the London Stock Exchange had rejected. The Euronext, it was said, has enough money to pay $ 1.4 billion. So far, neither bidder has presented an offer. But both of them would form the largest stock market operator in Europe, and the second largest in the world after the New York Stock Exchange. There was a rumor that the French would take advantage of the meeting on Friday to capitalize on the growing concern about the German's plans to take over the London Stock Exchange. The staff of the Deutsch Bourse in Frankfurt is allegedly concerned that if the takeover goes through, up to 300 jobs will be transferred to London. "The works council is concerned that the equities and derivatives exchange could later be run from London," a union source told Reuters. German politicians are said to be angry that the stock market operator had said that it would move to London if the offer was accepted. Meanwhile, LSE shareholders are afraid that the Deutsch Bourse, which controls the Clearstream unit that runs the trading settlement system, will create a monopoly and thus weaken the position of shareholders when negotiating lower stock trading fees. The London Stock Exchange and the Euronext have no control over their clearing and settlement system, a structure that is considered more transparent and competitive. Clearstream is considered the main obstacle to a merger between the London Stock Exchange and the Deutsch Bourse. According to some market experts, the Deutsch Bourse, which has now formally requested a decision from the German authorities on whether to take over the LSE, will offer to sell Clearstream to obtain the approval of shareholders. The Euronext has not yet given any hint of what kind of concessions it will offer the LSE, the largest stock exchange in Europe.

The shares of Bombardier, manufacturer of trains and aircraft, which fell to their lowest level in ten years after the departure of the chief executive officer and two members of the supervisory board, the mainstay of the company. The departure of Paul Tellier, who was also president of the company, was prompted by a reorganization of the company, which would now be under the leadership of Laurent Beaudoin, member of the family which controls the Montreal company. As for the observers, these resignations would seem to be due to a disagreement in the administration. Under the authority of Tellier, who had been at the head of the company since January 2003, it was decided to reduce by a third the workforce of 75,000 employees by 2006; the divisions of snowmobiles and defense were also sold, and the company was developing a new line of aircraft with 110 to 135 seats. Tellier had expressed the desire to stay at the head of the world's first manufacturer of passenger trains and third in civilian aircraft until the completion of the restructuring. But a drop in the share price, a drop in profits, was announced in the third quarter, which had seen profits fall from a yearly figure of a hundred and thirty-three million dollars. "I understand the worries of the board of directors that I would not be able to do so for a long time, and the need to develop and carry out a strategy, and the need to rearrange the administration. The company stated that the restructuring plans prepared by Tellier would continue to be carried out. The Bombardier shares fell by 0.65 of a dollar, or twenty-five percent, to the equivalent of $1.90, then climbed to $2.20.

Japan's growth evaporated in the third quarter, causing renewed worries about the economy that had just climbed out of a ten-year trough. During this period, production grew by only 0.1%, 0.3% on a yearly basis. Exports, the main engine of the recovery, did not recover, domestic demand remained sluggish, and capital expenditures remained at a low level. There was a new revival of the slump in the sluggish economy of the 1990s, albeit very limited and surrounded by periods of stagnation. Deflation, with falling prices, also made Japanese consumers cautious and prevented them from spending. During this crisis, the recovery of the economy became more dependent on exports. The soaring price of oil deducted 0.2% from the growth rate, and the depreciation of the yen made Japanese exports to the United States relatively more expensive. The third quarter was a reversal from the first half of the year. The first quarter had seen a yearly growth rate of 6.3%, the second, 1.1%, and economists had forecast that the third quarter would grow by as much as 2%. "Exports have slowed down and business spending has weakened," said Hiromichi Shirakawa, the chief economist of UBS Securities in Tokyo. “Consumer spending looks good, but this is partly due to temporary factors, such as the Olympic games.” The amber light was blinking. The Japanese government may have more difficulty raising taxes when the economy improves. To reduce the huge public debt, the economy needs to pick up.

After three years of reversals and fluctuations, the total profit of the three-gorges power company has more than doubled. Its profits are mainly driven by the strong demand for electricity, while the cost of coal is rising. The net profit in 2004 was three billion yuan, more than twice as much as that in 2003; the turnover rose to 6.2 billion yuan from three billion yuan. Although the turnover increased by only half that of last year, it still exceeded the forecast of many securities companies. The turnover will probably rise slightly in 2005, but it is expected to grow by only 20%. Three Gorges Bank Power Company is in urgent need of electricity to meet the needs of economic development; because the government has pushed back the construction of many power plants, and the economy is expected to heat up, the market is sluggish. This has led to the current high demand for electricity and the shortage of electricity. This month, because of the environment, three-gorges power station and the three-gorges Xiluodu power station and the three-gorges Xiluodu power plant, because of the environment, stopped construction; The whole country has also suspended more than 30 large-scale projects. In recent years, the three-gorges project has repressed more than 500,000 people, and has been under constant attack from the world and the public. The three-gorges Xiluodu project is under construction on the Jinsha River, also known as the upper reaches of the Yangtze River.

A new study by the United Nations Economic Commission for Europe indicates that the European Union's new member states will contribute a great deal to economic growth in Europe in 2005. The eight central European countries that joined the European Union last year are expected to see a 4.6% increase in their economies, while the twelve countries of the Eurozone will only see a 1.8% increase. The UNECE study also indicates that the world economy will slow down in 2005 because of weakening domestic demand, which could be further affected by efforts to reduce the current account deficit of the United States of America, which would lead to high exchange-rate volatility. The UNECE predicts that economic growth in the European Union will average 2.2% in 2005. But it also predicts that growth in the Eurozone will fall in 2004 from a projected 1.9% to 1.8%, largely because of a decline in the German economy, which shrank 0.2% in the last quarter of last year. According to the Bundesbank, the German economy will have a hard time achieving its goal of a 1.4% increase in 2005. The Bundesbank has also warned that the reduction of the budget deficit to below 3% of GDP poses a “huge risk”, especially in view of the fact that real growth is likely to be less than 0.5% this year. The UNECE has published its survey of the European economy for the year 2005, which indicates that central European countries such as the Czech Republic and Slovenia will again be the mainstay of the European economy, but smaller countries such as Cyprus, Ireland and Malta will also be among the best performers. The British economy, which grew 3.2% in 2004, will grow by only 2.5% in 2005, largely because of the fall in consumer demand. The UNECE also predicts that in many of Europe's largest economies, such as France, Germany and Italy, domestic demand will remain weak, which means that growth will be mainly driven by exports. “Given the fragility of domestic demand and the negative effects of the stronger euro on domestic demand and inflation, monetary policy in the Eurozone is likely to continue to be ‘wait and see',” the UNECE report says. While the economies of China and the United States of America are strong, the UNECE expects growth in the world economy to slow down from a projected 5% this year to 4.2%. The UNECE also warned that the American deficit would have to be brought under control, which would pose a challenge for policymakers in both the United States and other countries.

These railroads, which were closed in 1969, will be opened to the public on the 15th of this month. The anniversary of the closing of the line which ran from Edinburgh to Carlisle is to be marked by a walk along the line, which was closed at Tweedbank on the 6th of that month. MSPs are to consider whether to reintroduce rail services from Midlothian to the Scottish Borders. Reopening the Waverley Line would cost up to £100 million, but it is claimed that it would give the Borders an economic lift. In 2000 the council said that since the railroads had been closed the local economy had suffered. Campaign for Borders rail, a lobby group, said that it was determined to keep the pressure on the Scottish government. “We are planning a walk along the railway line to mark the 36th anniversary of the closing of the Waverley Line,” said Ms Borthwick. “Campaign for Borders rail is the biggest independent campaign group in Scotland and has been urging the Scottish government to bring the railway back to the Borders and eventually to Carlisle.” Ms Borthwick said that the Scottish government must commit to the first phase of the project by pledging to fund the line between Edinburgh and Tweedbank at first and then to investigate the possibility of extending the line in the future. Reopening the line would be a good investment, said Ms Borthwick, and would help to protect the Borders’ identity. A study carried out in 2000, which was commissioned by the Scottish government, Scottish Borders Council, Midlothian Council and Scottish Borders Enterprise, showed that a train every half-hour from Tweedbank to Edinburgh would cover its costs. It also found that a half-hourly service from Gorebridge to Edinburgh would cover its costs and that a freight line connecting to the west coast main line at Longtown would also be viable.

The BBC News website looks at how the world of mobile phone games is growing. A brief summary follows, but you can jump to the reviews by clicking on the links below. Part 2 follows on Monday. Reviews of Call of Duty, Splinter Cell - Pandora Tomorrow, The Lord of the Rings and Pocket Kingdom will follow on Monday. If you imagine Snake when you hear about mobile phone games, you could be in for a surprise. This is because the world of mobile phone games has come a long way in a short space of time. Even before the N-Gage game phone was launched in November 2003, operators realised that there were lots of people who wanted to play games on their phones. Because mobile phones are much more common than dedicated gaming devices such as the GameBoy, it was a potentially very profitable market. And the audience for mobile games includes a wide variety of people - from people looking for something to do on the way home from work, to people who like playing games in their spare time. And over the last year, life has become much easier for all these people, because the number of titles you can get on your phone has soared. Now, a review of games on a mobile phone operator's site by Wireless Game Review has a list of more than 200 titles available from a single network, and there is a wide variety of titles available. There are versions of games you would expect to find on the PC or consoles, such as Space Invaders and Bejewelled. There are action games, puzzle games and strategy games, as well as many games that are unique to the mobile phone. It is now unusual for a film to be released these days without a game based on it. These games are becoming an important part of a film's marketing campaign - not surprising when you think that a good game can get many millions of downloads. They can also be very profitable - some cost up to £5. One of the things that has helped the mobile games industry grow is that they are now easier to get hold of - technology called WAP push. By sending a text message to a game provider, you can get it downloaded to your phone. Just a few short months ago, you had to go through several layers of menus on most operator sites. The number of phones that can play these games has also increased dramatically. Now, nearly half of all phones are capable of running the more sophisticated games that are available - even the 3D games. The minimum technology that mobile phones need to have is getting more sophisticated, which means that games are getting more sophisticated too. With more processing power, the physics in games are becoming more convincing, and the visuals are also improving. Also, some games are beginning to make use of the network. Many of the newer racing games let you post your best times to a central scoring system, so you can see how you are doing compared to other players. Usually you can get hold of the best times others have posted, and race against them as a ghost. Another kind of game lets you compete against other people, either through the network or, if you are in the same place, via short-range radio technology called Bluetooth. There is so much happening in the world of mobile games, it is difficult to give a full picture of the various things that are going on. Hopefully, these two features have given you an idea of what is available, and how you can get involved. Even as I begin playing Too Fast Too Furious, I remember why I don't play driving games: I'm rubbish at them. No matter whether I'm using the d-pad or the joystick, I can't manage to stop the car in time for the corners or make it overtake. I have to do this over and over again - the time limit for each section of the track is constantly being reduced. For some reason, the visuals are quite involving, with palm trees and cacti flying past, and the city in the background scrolling along. The cars are surprisingly easy to drive, even with my rubbish driving skills, but it's not clear whether the different models are significantly different in handling. If you win, you can spend the money you've won on new equipment. The only downside is the rather clunky menus, which are especially annoying if you use the joystick rather than the numeric keypad. Fatal Force is a futuristic shooter that lets you play a series of death matches against the phone, or a campaign, in which you have to stop an alien invasion. The visuals are a bit comical, but that makes it easier to see what's going on, and the level design makes it tempting to explore. The music and sound effects are well done, the campaigns are well written, and you get help from the commanders at key points. You get flamethrowers, rocket launchers, grenades and even get to use a robot for a short while. You can use power-ups to enter bullet-time and slow down the aliens' attacks. You can also compete with other people, using Bluetooth, if they are in range. On the web, there are clans, leaderboards and even new levels that you can download.

Sony's PSP is the UK's top gadget of 2005, according to a roundup of the most indispensable gizmos compiled by Stuff magazine. It beats the iPod to the second place in the top ten essentials list, which reveals the favourites of the gadget-lovers this year. Buying all ten gadgets will cost you £7,455. That is £1,000 less than the previous year, because of a reduction in manufacturing costs, which have made gizmos cheaper. The portables dominated the list, including the Sharp 902 phone, the Pentax Optio SV digital camera and the Yepp YH-999 digital music player. "What this year's essentials show is that gadgets are cheaper, sexier and more indispensable than ever before. We've got to the point where you can't live without them," said Adam Vaughan, editor of Stuff Essentials. "As they creep into our homes and take over our lives, the high street is being transformed." And who needs to go to a record shop when you can legally download a song in minutes for less than a pound? " The new technology will be capturing the imagination of gadget lovers in the next year, the survey concludes. The Xbox 2, high-definition televisions and MP3 mobile phones will be among the most in-demand gadgets in 2006, the survey predicts. The release of the PSP in the UK in the spring is eagerly awaited by gaming fans.

The man who boasted of having launched The Aviator and got Leonardo DiCaprio the rôle of the hero, has been shut out of the nominations for the Academy. Charles Evans Jr. fought a long battle with the film-makers who eventually produced the picture, and obtained a production credit, but he is not nominated for an Academy award as a producer. Two of the four producers who worked on the film are nominated. Only three producers are allowed to share in a film, and as the film-makers for The Aviator and Million-Dollar Baby could not settle on a trio, the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences has decided to trim the list for them. Michael Mann and Graham King are the nominees for The Aviator, while Charles Evans Jr. and Sandy Climan, who was the second to Michael Mann, are not nominated. Evans had brought suit against Mann in 2001, claiming that he had originated the idea, spent years developing it, and had pushed DiCaprio into the rôle of Howard Hughes, but that he had been dropped from the picture.
